headline: Kai, the market comes back from the long weekend to $99 Brent, fresh Canadian tariffs at the border, and a Fed eight days from choosing a hike.
subline: Futures are steady to lower, hike odds hold near 60 percent into Friday's CPI, and bitcoin sits near $79,000 after another rejection at $82,000.
asof: Pre-market · as of 6:45 AM ET · index values are futures · every figure links to its source below

items.title: Futures tilt lower as the week reopens
items.sentence: Dow futures are off 0.5 percent and S&P 500 futures 0.2 percent while Nasdaq futures hold slightly green in the first session since Friday's jobs-driven slide, per Investing.com.

items.title: Warsh keeps a September hike alive
items.sentence: Markets put the odds of a quarter-point hike at next Wednesday's decision near 60 percent, and Chair Kevin Warsh has said underlying inflation trends have not meaningfully improved, per Marketplace.

items.title: Brent probes $99, a six-week high
items.sentence: Brent rose about 2 percent to $99.32 on Tuesday, up 13 percent in a month, after weekend strikes on tankers from both sides of the strait, per Trading Economics.

items.title: Quiet data today, CPI waits on Friday
items.sentence: Today brings NFIB small-business optimism, consumer inflation expectations, a 3-year note auction and July consumer credit, with August PPI due Thursday and CPI Friday at a 3.4 percent consensus, per Trading Economics.

items.title: Bitcoin backs off $82,000 again
items.sentence: Bitcoin trades near $79,000 after a fourth rejection at $82,000 since late August — still up about 23 percent from its August 7 low but 10 percent below January's open — ahead of the Senate's September 15 CLARITY Act vote, per 24/7 Wall St.

items.title: Canada's counter-tariffs take effect this morning
items.sentence: Ottawa's tariffs of 15 to 50 percent on $27.6 billion of US goods — steel, aluminum, dairy and electronics among them — answered Washington's 50 percent Section 338 duties at 12:01 a.m. today, per Mohawk Global.

items.title: Tanker war tightens the Strait of Hormuz
items.sentence: The US hit three Iranian oil tankers and Iran struck six vessels including US-linked ships over the weekend, leaving roughly ten commodity ships a day crossing a strait that normally carries a fifth of the world's oil, per Al Jazeera.

items.title: Kyiv talks substantive, but no deal
items.sentence: Witkoff and Kushner met Zelenskyy in Kyiv after seeing Putin in Moscow, with Washington now pressing for trilateral talks, per Al Jazeera.

items.title: Five dead in Miami cargo-plane overrun
items.sentence: An Amazon Prime Air freighter overran a Miami International runway Sunday and struck a van, killing five, and the NTSB investigation is underway, per NPR.

items.title: AfD doubles its vote in Saxony-Anhalt
items.sentence: The far-right AfD more than doubled its vote share to finish first in Sunday's Saxony-Anhalt state election, a result NPR calls a historic victory.

items.title: OpenAI's Astra keeps chip stocks running
items.sentence: Samsung rose 3.9 percent and SK Hynix 5.5 percent Monday after Jensen Huang said GPT-6 Astra was trained on more than 100,000 Nvidia systems with 400,000 more GPUs to come, per Bloomingbit.

items.title: Anthropic books a fall IPO window
items.sentence: The Claude maker is targeting September or October at a post-money valuation near $965 billion, with Morgan Stanley, Goldman Sachs and JPMorgan running the book, per Yahoo Finance.

items.title: Samsung leads Mistral's record €3 billion
items.sentence: Europe's largest-ever equity round, announced Tuesday, values the French lab above €21 billion, per Euronews.

items.title: NHTSA opens Cybercab compliance probe
items.sentence: Tesla fell about 6 percent Friday after the safety regulator announced an investigation into Cybercab compliance, per Yahoo Finance.

items.title: Google begins one-way swap to Gemini
items.sentence: Google started replacing Assistant with Gemini across Android, Wear OS and cars on September 4, a rollout with no option to revert, per AI Weekly.
